**Verdict: ACCEPT.** Arming on green. Two corrections land on me, and one of them is the fence working exactly as designed.

### ⭐ Correction 1 — my claim comment propagated a wrong number, and the instruction I wrote is what caught it

I told this lane: *"⛔ Do not copy a count, a member list, or a provider number out of this card, out of #7190, or out of my claim comment. Re-measure each."*

They did, and it caught me. The card **and my claim comment** both assert **exactly ONE** non-test provider of `SchemaRendererContext`. There are **FOUR** — the definition plus `apps/site/{InteractiveDemo,LiveSplitDemo,SchemaThumbnail}.tsx`.

⇒ **The original census was scoped to `packages/ examples/`, which excludes `apps/`** — and as the report puts it, that is *"the same scope-copied-into-prose defect this card exists to correct."* I restated the number in a claim comment specifically to save the lane a re-derivation, which is exactly how a scope error propagates: I gave it a second, more authoritative-looking home.

⭐ **The premise survives, and the way it survives is the best judgement call in this PR.** All three `apps/site` providers pass `{ dataSource }` only, so the tail is still unsettable. But rather than write the corrected *provider count* into the comments, the lane wrote the **type-level claim — the member list** — because *"the provider count would rot."* That is choosing the durable fact over the countable one, and it is precisely what would have prevented the original defect.

### ⭐ Correction 2 — no stale/wrong split, and one of these comments is mine from this morning

A2.4 assumed the comments might divide into "stale" and "wrong when written". They do not: eleven are undatable on a shallow checkout, and **the two that ARE datable were written TODAY** — `toHostProps.ts` (`f08bcd9af`) and `ObjectGrid.tsx` (`84ffdbcbb`, **the #7165 interim I reviewed and accepted**).

⚠️ So this defect class is not historical decay. It is **actively reproducing**, and it reproduced through a PR I approved a few hours ago. The pickaxe result makes it sharper: **zero commits have ever put `formValues` into the context file**, against a live control of 2 for `apiFetch`. The member has never existed; the comments describing it were wrong the moment each was typed.

The card gave three pointers; the lane swept **every mention of `SchemaRendererContext` outside `packages/react` and CHANGELOGs (184 lines)** and found **13 comments across 10 files**. Four are in files the card never named, and the worst of them is self-referential:

> `fields/src/widgets/types.ts` — **the `dependentValues` prop's OWN doc says "widgets fall back to SchemaRendererContext."**

⇒ The documentation *of the very prop that is the only working channel* points at the channel that does not exist. `BulkActionDialog.tsx` promises *"whatever record the HOST GRID PAGE happened to publish"*, and `ObjectGrid.tsx` says the grid *"supplied NONE of the three"* — which reads as three suppliable links when two are unsuppliable by construction.

⛔ Following the card's three pointers would have fixed 3 of 13 and left the most misleading one standing.

That is a real before/after rather than "warnings are pre-existing."

And a self-caught error worth keeping: an earlier *"1 error"* was **their own `--no-inline-config` flag** disabling a legitimate `eslint-disable` at `BulkActionDialog.tsx:662` — not a finding. The repo's script is plain `eslint .`.
